metadata.title: Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting in Internal Fluid Flow

configuration.quote: A piezoelectric bimorph connected in parallel (QP21B produced by Mide Technology Corporation, Medford, MA, USA [26]) was used to demonstrate power generation in our first flow energy harvester design.

proof_mass.quote: A piezoelectric bimorph connected in parallel (QP21B produced by Mide Technology Corporation, Medford, MA, USA [26]) was used to demonstrate power generation in our first flow energy harvester design.

length_mm.quote: total length and width are 1.63 inch (42.418 mm) and 0.67 inch 17.018 mm, respectively.

width_mm.quote: total length and width are 1.63 inch (42.418 mm) and 0.67 inch 17.018 mm, respectively.

thickness_mm.quote: The total thickness is 0.031 inch (0.7874 mm).

substrate_thickness_um.quote: 0.002 inch (0.0508 mm) stainless steel shim was added to either side of the commercially available QP21B bimorph actuator

piezo_thickness_um.quote: two thin 0.008 inch (0.2032 mm) of PZT5A type piezoelectric elements

type.quote: Fluid motion is coupled to structural vibration via a cantilever beam placed in a converging-diverging flow channel.

frequency_Hz.quote: first resonant frequency ... decreases to around 140 Hz in water.

displacement_mm.quote: max deflection of this bimorph is found to be on the order of 2 mm

load_resistance_ohm.quote: optimal electrical resistance at 140 Hz in water is between 7 and 10 kOhm.

resonant_frequency_Hz.quote: first resonant frequency ... decreases to around 140 Hz in water.

output_power_W.quote: output power with all tested nozzle-diffuser inserts showed the same maximum of 25 mW

open_circuit_voltage_V.quote: open circuit voltage of 20 V at a tip deflection of 0.18 mm
